chapter: England, later career and closing thoughts
title: Variety houses, Lew Grade's circle and fan Alan Hobbs
summary: She played a week at a time plus Sunday variety shows in London, met the Grade brothers and agent Mumford, and a young fan Alan Hobbs followed her tour.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, what I'd do, I'd work six days in one place and on Sundays we'd come to London and do -- I think they called it variety. They called it variety there. I think that's the name they called it, variety. Variety houses and variety concerts. But it was really variety, because you know

it was just something like our vaudeville shows here that we used to have, where they had comedians, you know, and dancers and singers and just all sorts of acts on the show, you know. It was just marvelous.

But it was a marvelous experience, and I got to know Lew Grade and Leslie, and Delfonte, who's a big man. In fact I think Delfonte was kind of responsible for my going over the first time, through an agent, Mumford, I think this guy's name was, Mumford. I think that's his name. I hope I remember the name correctly.

But anyway, Delfonte is a brother to the Grades. You know, they're all brothers, and they're all in different capacities, you know. But it was a marvelous, wonderful, wonderful experience, and as I say, today I hear from people, I still hear from them, and this young fellow whose name is Alan Hobbs, he's the little fellow who followed us all around, well he's now in California. He's been here for quite some time. He lives in San Francisco. So he keeps in touch and he goes back home. I guess his parents are still living in England, and he goes home about every year or every other year or so, and he keeps in constant touch with me.
